item.title: Self-Hosted Network Routing Protocol Monitoring: FRRouting vs BIRD vs GoBGP (2026)
item.description: Running a self-hosted routing infrastructure requires visibility into protocol state, peer connectivity, and route advertisements. Three open-source routing suites dominate the space: FRRouting (FRR), BIRD, and GoBGP. Each provides a different approach to routing protocol implementation, monitoring, and operational management.

item.title: Self-Hosted OSPF Monitoring: FRRouting vs BIRD vs GoBGP OSPF Tools (2026)
item.description: Open Shortest Path First (OSPF) is the most widely deployed interior gateway protocol (IGP) in enterprise and service provider networks. Monitoring OSPF adjacencies, link-state advertisements (LSAs), and routing table changes is critical for network operations teams who need to detect neighbor flaps, suboptimal routing, and topology changes before they impact production traffic.
